Let’s get started

We suggest working through these in order, starting with your guest list. You can jump to any step, and come back here any time from Project → What to do next.

1. Create your guest list Start here Most of Tableau is built from your guest list, so this is the best place to begin.
  1. aDownload the free Excel template.
  2. bFill it in on your computer: names, groups, cell numbers and any wedding roles. Keep the columns as they are.
  3. cImport your completed list into Tableau.
Prefer to type them in? Add guests one by one.

Create your guest list

Bring your guests in from an Excel list, or type them in one by one. You can add more any time.

1. Download the templateAn Excel file with the columns we need. Fill in your guests’ names and groups, then save it.
2. Import your listChoose your filled-in file. It must use the same columns as our template, otherwise names may not come in correctly.
Or add guests one by oneType each name in and choose a group. Good for small lists or last-minute additions.

Wedding checklist

    Group photos

    • Name each photo and add a time and place.
    • Pick the guests in it and add their WhatsApp number.
    • Tap WhatsApp to tell them beforehand.
    • Phone numbers stay private. They never appear on the guest or bridal party pages.
    • The bridal party page shows photo names and who is in them.
    • Keep it short: 10 to 20 minutes in total.
    • Ask someone who knows everyone to gather people (the “wrangler”).
    • Biggest groups first, then take people out.
    • Seat grandparents near shade or chairs.

    Drag, drop, and set the perfect tone.

    Your whole wedding day in one place: seat your guests, design the room, plan the day with your bridal party, and share one QR code with your guests.

    Tip: Tableau works best on a computer. On a phone, seating works but the floor plan does not yet.

    How it works

    1. 1
      Free sign-up FreeCreate an account for free, or play around on the site first.
    2. 2
      Guest list FreeCreate your guest list or import it from Excel (free template to download inside). Everything else is pulled from this list.
    3. 3
      Seat your guests FreeDrag and drop names onto round, rectangle or U-shaped tables.
    4. 4
      Design the room FreeBuild a floor plan to scale. Guests get a simple map with a key on their phones.
    5. 5
      One QR code FreeGuests scan it, find their name and see their table marked with a red star. Try a live example on your phone.
    6. 6
      Make it yours FreeAdd your photo, date, colours and style, all saved to your account.
    7. 7
      Menu, programme and gifts An add-on to your QR guest page. Upload your menu, programme and banking details so guests have them right on their phones (Canva templates available). See a live example on your phone.
    8. 8
      Bridal party page Jobs, packing lists and vendor contacts on a private link.
    9. 9
      Vendors and group photos Keep every contact in one place, plan each group photo and WhatsApp the guests in it.
    10. 10
      The whole weekend Add a day before and a day after, each with its own programme.

    Steps 1 to 6 are free. Steps 7 to 10 are optional paid plans: Guest page R100 a year, Full planner R200 a year. See what each plan includes

    Photos & videos from guests

    Step by step: how do I make a shared album and get the link?
    1. Create the shared album
    1. Open the Google Photos app, or go to photos.google.com.
    2. Tap Library or Albums at the bottom, then New album (or the + icon).
    3. Type a clear title, for example “Sarah & Mark’s Wedding”.
    4. Tap Share at the top right.
    5. Tap Create link (or Get link) to make the web address.
    2. Let guests add their own photos
    1. Open your new shared album and tap the three dots (…) or the Settings icon at the top right.
    2. Choose Options or Sharing options.
    3. Switch Collaborate (“Let others add photos and videos”) ON.
    4. Copy the album link and paste it into the box above. Guests will get a button on your guest page that opens it, so you do not need a separate QR code. (If you would like one on table cards anyway, paste the link into a free QR code maker such as Adobe Express.)
    3. What guests do
    1. Tap the button on your guest page, or scan a QR code, to open the album on their phone.
    2. Sign in to their Google account if asked.
    3. Tap Join at the top of the album.
    4. Tap the Add photos icon (the + with a photo), choose their photos and tap Add or Done.
    Anyone with the link can add photos and videos, but cannot delete yours. Everything goes straight into your own Google account, so it does not use any Tableau storage.
    Google Drive instead? Create a folder, click Share, set General access to Anyone with the link, choose Editor, and copy the link. Editors can also delete files, so Google Photos is the safer choice.

    Bridal party page

    • A private page for your bridal party.
    • Each person taps their name and sees only their own jobs, with what to do now and next, plus their packing list.
    • Start with a ready-made list, then change anything.
    • Tap a heading to open or close a section.

    The day

    Who is who

    • List everyone who has jobs.
    • A job shows for a person if its Who matches their name or role. Use roles like “Best Man” and add the real names here.
    • Phone numbers can be typed any usual way (083 276 9190 or +27 83 276 9190). They give tap-to-call and WhatsApp buttons.

    What to pack

    • A separate checklist so nobody forgets something important, including honeymoon bags.
    • Each item has a What, a Who and a When (“The day before” or a date like “12 Oct”).
    • Items already on the list are never added twice.
    Start from a ready-made list
    WhatWhoWhen

    Big Day jobs

    • This is the one master list of everything on the day. Each job appears once.
    • Two ways to start: let the app assign ready-made jobs to the right person or role, or add them unassigned and do it yourself.
    • To give a job to a role, tap the arrow under Who and tick the roles (or use Jobs by role below).
    • A job can belong to several roles.
    TimeJobWhoWhere

    Jobs by role

    • One card per role, showing its jobs.
    • Cards stay empty until you pick jobs from Big Day jobs, add that role’s ready-made jobs, or add a new job.
    • Taking a job off a role does not delete it. It stays in Big Day jobs.
